title: Python: attribute-write follow-ups — the defining module's own f() and the dotted/instance write shapes (DEC-303 a79 Q-B, Q-C)
description: Record-only follow-up under DEC-303 (a79) (opum-ai/opum-doc#2082, ODOC-640). Two groups, both wrong edges confirmed by measurement, both NOT built in GCLI-140/#233: (Q-B) the defining module's own bare call after an importer writes its attribute — in m.py, def f() and def g() calling f(), with app.py doing m.f = other: a bare f() in m reads m's globals, which m.f = other writes, so the edge is wrong (dev and #233 both give it). (Q-C) every F7 shape, each a write inside the analysed modules and so a wrong edge, not a blind spot: dotted class targets (Outer.Inner.m = v, app.D.m = v reachable through an import; the from-import twin already refuses because the class name has two bindings), type(self).m = v and self.__class__.m = v (recorded as nothing), from m import inst; inst.m = v; inst.m() (importedInstanceClass has no write check), and a subclass's self.m = v leaving a base's self.m() resolving (the MRO guard walks the receiver's MRO, not its descendants). HELD under the (a49) item 7 hold list ((a50) item 3). ORDER: right after #233 lands, ahead of GCLI-141 to 143; the (a36) item 8 pre-registration waits for it. Proof: red-before/green-after fixtures per shape with resolving twins, a mutant per path observed red, removal-only proved by the subset check over the five pins, the fixtures and the corpus, two review rounds under DEC-161; any created in-repo edge comes to opum-doc before the PR. Any shape that is not small comes to opum-doc before it is built.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The defining module’s own bare f() after an importer writes m.f refuses, with a red-before/green-after fixture and a mutant per path

Each Q-C shape (Outer.Inner.m, app.D.m through an import, type(self).m, self.__class__.m, from m import inst; inst.m = v, a subclass write reaching a base’s self.m()) has a refused fixture, a resolving twin and a mutant
Removal-only is proved by the subset check over the five pins, the fixtures and the corpus, and every created in-repo edge is reported to opum-doc before the PR
No shape is widened past (a79); any non-small shape comes to opum-doc before it is built

plan: 1. Scope the record on dev 719cec5b: the description Q-B/Q-C shapes are landed by GCLI-154/155/159/156/163/164; the open wrong edge is note 4 (descendant __class__ write).
2. Guard: descendantClassWritten used by methodLookup instance dispatch and the bare self.m() path; bump PYTHON_ANALYZER_VERSION to 5.
3. Fixtures: note 4 (annotation, parameter, self, R4, constructed, neighbour, class-level and unrelated twins) red-before/green-after, a mutant per path observed red.
4. Note 3: the two fail-closed super fixtures and the B1 loop as test.each; N-a/N-b/N-c pins.
5. Proof kit over five pins, 1394-source corpus and fixtures at the exact new floor; created = 0, removed edges listed.
6. Close GCLI-168 in the same PR.
implementationNotes:
REVIEWER N ITEMS AND (a80) CARRIES (opum-doc DEC-303 (a80), opum-ai/opum-doc#2083, ODOC-640). This task takes all of the following; it goes right after #233 lands, ahead of GCLI-141 to 143, and the (a36) item 8 pre-registration waits for it. If the task cannot fit two rounds, split it BEFORE building into a binder-side and a read-side held task, both holding the pre-registration, and say so; no further ruling is needed for the split.
(a80) CARRIES — the mod.f gate is OFF in two positions in #233 so they behave exactly as on dev, leaving their wrong edges here: a written class name in a BASE position (class D(m.C) with m.C = other) and in a TWO-ARGUMENT super() first argument (super(m.C, self).m() and the from-import twin), where the enclosing-class fallback resolves dev's m.py:A.m and #233 keeps app.py:B.m (B1, B1b); and dev's own enclosing-class fallback for any unresolved super() first argument, a wrong edge of its own whose removed edges go to opum-doc when it is fixed.
N1: a class name assigned through another name: K = C; K.m = other does not land on C; and the module-alias shape import m; n = m; n.f = other, and k = cls; k.m = g, k = type(self); k.m = other — none recorded.
N2: import m; m.f = other; from m import *; f() still resolves through resolveStarBound (calls.ts:2716) — the star path does not read the module write.
N3: classSymbolOfName (calls.ts:4311) bypasses the gate: from m import C and m.C = other, then h = C.m; h(), and an R4 local x = C(); x.m(), still resolve.
N4: a decorator @C.m after C.m = other still resolves (calls.ts:3404) — the decorator path does not read the class write.
N5: del C.m and del self.m count as writes, as GCLI-115 counts del for names.
N6: a missed C.__init__ refusal (calls.ts:3780) — the construction path does not consult the write. Its over-refusal twin (self.__call__ = f refusing x(), when implicit dunders look the method up on the type) is RECALL and is the separate ordinary task GCLI-153, not this one.
N7: __init__ writing self.__class__ = Other leaves OUTSIDE receivers (x = C(); x.m() in another module) resolving — the class write is recorded, the cross-module receiver is not refused.
N8: diamond super — MEASURED on dev 57ba445 and on #233's head, both: with class A(def m), B(A) whose m calls super().m(), C(A)(def m), D(B, C), the call D().m() gives the edge app.py:6:9 -> app.py:A.m while a D instance's super() after B reaches C.m. A WRONG EDGE on dev and head, so it joins this task.
Proof required: red-before/green-after fixtures per shape with resolving twins, a mutant per path observed red, and removal-only by the subset check over the five pins, the fixtures and the corpus (flags included); two review rounds under DEC-161; any created in-repo edge comes to opum-doc via the leader before the PR.

SPLIT FILED 2026-11-27 under DEC-303 (a80) item 6 (records only): this task is the umbrella. GCLI-154 is the binder-side half (#2 dotted class targets, #3 module-global class rebinding m.C = other, #4 type(self)/__class__ writes, #11 N1 aliases, #15 del); GCLI-155 is the read-side one-path half (#1, #5, #7, #8, #9, #10, #12, #13, #14, #16), depends on GCLI-154; GCLI-156 is the heavy half (#6, #17, #18) and waits for an opum-doc ruling. Order GCLI-154, then GCLI-155, then GCLI-156; all three keep hold, hold the (a36) item 8 pre-registration, and come ahead of GCLI-141 to 143. Dev results measured 2026-11-27 at origin/dev 1ea3432 are in each record.

RE-CARRIED from GCLI-164 (#250 round 1, B2): GCLI-164 closed without carrying these watch items, so they land here as open items, not as builds — scope each before building. N-f: cls.__class__.m is a measured removal-only over-refusal (test/python-hops.test.ts ~:3089); accepted by (a84), still unfixed. N-a: a write recorded on a MIXIN is invisible to the #6 descendant guard (class C(B, Mix), Mix writes self.m). N-b: a class-body binding on a descendant (class C(B): m = 2) is neither a recorded write nor a def, so the guard does not see it. N-c: c = C(); c.m = 2 goes to addLocalAttrWrite, not classAttrWrites. N-e: removal-only over-refusals on B().m(), x = B(); x.m(), B.m(o), h = B.m; h(), and f = B(); f() (__call__) never see a descendant instance and fall back to a name bin, unfixtured. BLIND SPOT from #250 round 1 item 5: a type(self).m write in a NESTED def is not attributed to the receiver because receiverOfIgnoringMisparse stops at the inner scope holding the marked misparse binding; dev-equal, pinned, not fixed.

FROM DEC-303 (a90) item 2 (opum-ai/opum-doc#2104), after glyph-cli#250 landed: this task carries the fail-closed fixtures the GCLI-164 record names as a documented limitation. (1) :3891 `at < 0` fixture: A.m; B(A) defined twice (so the base name is bound twice); class D(B) with B.m calling super().m() refuses where dev gives A.m — and note the same path refuses under single inheritance, not only the diamond. Mutant observed red: the fixture plus a mutant that removes the `return true` at `at < 0` must turn it red. (2) :3887 `!mro.ok` fixture, where one can be built. (3) test.each split: turn the B1 shape loop (setattr / del / augmented / metaclass) into test.each cases so each shape reports separately and M30 red subset is per-shape. Scope each before building; none is part of a current build.

CARRY from GCLI-163 round 1 (DEC-303 (a88)), named here, NOT built: a descendant __class__ write is missed for annotation and parameter receivers. classAttributeWritten walks the receiver's ANCESTORS only, so `def f(x: C): x.m()` still resolves when a `class D(C)` writes `self.__class__` in its __init__, because an instance of D is not in C's ancestor MRO. The bare self.m() path at the same guard has the same gap on dev (a descendant writing __class__ is invisible to it). Both predate GCLI-163 and lie outside shape #17, which fixes only the ancestor-covered cases. A fix needs the descendant relation on the instance path (descendantsOf), the way shape #6 does it. Scope before building.

ROUND-2 REVIEWER NON-BLOCKING GAPS from GCLI-141 / opum-ai/glyph-cli#255 (DEC-303 (a28)/(a91)), carried here, NOT built: (i) The differently-named re-export CYCLE fixture is cut in S3 at modules.ts:1242 and never reaches the broadened predicate, so its termination rests on MAX_MODULE_DEPTH, not on the new path; and GCLI-141's record wording "(target in helper.py)" is inaccurate — pkg/helper.py is only a decoy and is not reached by that fixture. (ii) Refused twin (a)'s mutation sensitivity — dropping the calls.ts:3004 __init__ exclusion — is PREDICTED, not OBSERVED: no mutant was run against twin (a) (the source-null-guard mutant was run against twin (b) and python-calls.test.ts:1875). (iii) GCLI-141 note 1's stale "still treats a from-import binding as a module" sentence is RETAINED, with the ROUND-2 note as its correction rather than an in-place deletion — so a reader of note 1 alone reads a false claim. (iv) The refused twins and the cycle assert bins but not `reasons`, so a bin-only assertion could pass on a different refusal reason (module-called vs import-cycle vs run-time-bound are unasserted).

BUILD AND PROOF (round 1, 2026-11-27). Scope: the record's note 4 only, cleared by the leader. The description's Q-B/Q-C shapes are already landed (GCLI-154, 155, 159, 156, 163, 164); I re-measured Q-B and the imported-instance shape on dev 719cec5b and both refuse with resolving twins.

Change: descendantClassWritten(classInfo, name) consults the in-repo descendants' classAttrWrites. It is used by methodLookup's instance-dispatch guard (annotated and parameter receivers, the R4 local, the imported instance, the constructed receiver, __call__) and by the bare self.m() path. Removal-only; a descendant outside the analysed modules stays the accepted blind spot. PYTHON_ANALYZER_VERSION 4 -> 5 per its docstring (a79 Q-D).

Fixtures (test/python-hops.test.ts, 8 note-4 tests): annotation, parameter, bare self, R4, constructed, neighbour + class-level twin, unrelated-class twin. Red-before on dev: 6 of 8 fail (the class-level and unrelated twins pass, as they must). Mutants observed red: M1 disabling the methodLookup descendant guard turned exactly the five methodLookup shapes red (annotation, parameter, R4, constructed, neighbour) and left the self test and both twins green; M2 disabling the bare-self guard turned exactly the bare-self test red. Note 3: two fail-closed super fixtures added. The at<0 fixture from the record could NOT be isolated: removing `if (at < 0) return true` does not turn it red because the second-B-binding shape is served by the !mro.ok branch; the test says so and the at<0 branch stays defensive. The B1 shape loop is now test.each (4 cases). N-a/N-b/N-c pin fixtures added (measured fixed on dev; twins resolve B.m, B.m, C.m).

PROOF KIT (grown kit at /Volumes/external/archive/glyph-cli/gcli-161-proof-kit, four GCLI-151 fixtures added): dev 719cec5b vs head d3c3f7b over five pins + 1394 corpus sources + 166 fixtures = 1565 groups, exact floor 1565. 0 created, 0 flag-changed, pins unchanged edge for edge (flask 1366, httpx 2791, jinja 2833, rich 7410, tqdm 981); 4 removed edges and 4 bin changes, all four in the new GCLI-151 fixtures, named: annotation app.py:11:5->app.py:C.m; R4 app.py:12:5->C.m; constructed app.py:11:5->C.m; self receiver app.py:8:9->C.m. The GCLI-141 fixtures show no delta (dev already carries GCLI-141), so the whole delta is the four new fixtures. Controls: --control reported both injected created edges; --floor-control failed at 1e6; constructorNotes identical on all 1565 groups (9 with notes, 1559 notes), and its control reported the injected difference. Full suite 1416 pass, 0 fail; typecheck, lint, format:check clean.

GCLI-168 closed in the same PR (its four ACs evidenced; #260 and #261 cited in its final summary).

ROUND 2 (DEC-303 (a94), the last round; one commit on 935ca56). Applied verbatim:
Item 1, narrowing: descendantClassWritten now runs only for an ANNOTATED or parameter receiver (knownClassOf reports which arm matched) and for the bare self.m() path. Constructed C().m(), the R4 local, the imported instance and x = C(); x() keep resolving as on dev; the constructed and R4 note-4 tests are flipped to resolving pins and the describe comment no longer claims them.
Item 2, (2a): localClassOfReceiver consults descendant __class__ writes, so k = type(self); k.m() and k = self.__class__; k.m() refuse after a descendant's write. (2b): descendantClassWritten walks each descendant's MRO, a mixin included, and fails closed on !mro.ok.
Item 5: the GCLI-156 #6 loop is NOT changed; its over-refusal and the same mixin gap are filed as the ordinary follow-up GCLI-171.
PYTHON_ANALYZER_VERSION stays 5.

Fixtures: refused twins for annotation, parameter and self; resolving pins for constructed, R4, imported instance and __call__; new 2a (both forms), 2b mixin, cross-module annotation, two-level descendant, setattr(self, "__class__", X) and the retitled second !mro.ok fixture (its at<0 mutant is unmet). 18 GCLI-151 tests. Mutants: M4 disabling the localClassOfReceiver descendant check turned exactly the two 2a tests red; M5 restoring own-writes-only turned exactly the 2b mixin test red. Full suite 1423 pass, 0 fail; typecheck, lint, format:check clean.

PROOF KIT, dev 719cec5b vs head 4d623a4, current kit (169 fixtures): 1568 groups, exact floor 1568, exit 0. 0 created, 0 flag-changed; five pins unchanged edge for edge (flask 1366, httpx 2791, jinja 2833, rich 7410, tqdm 981); dev 17626 edges, head 17621. Five removed edges and five bin changes, exactly the set the ruling accepted in advance:
  annotation app.py:11:5->app.py:C.m, bins receiverNeedsInference 0->1
  self receiver app.py:8:9->app.py:C.m, bins 0->1
  2a type(self) app.py:9:9->app.py:C.m, bins 0->1 (resolvedExternal 1 stays)
  2a self.__class__ app.py:9:9->app.py:C.m, bins 0->1
  2b mixin app.py:13:5->app.py:C.m, bins 0->1
No corpus or pin removal. Controls: --control reported both injected created edges; --floor-control failed at 1e6; constructorNotes identical on all 1568 groups and its control reported the injection. The R4 and constructed pins resolve on both sides, so the round-1 over-removal is gone.
